blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Home Extension Cost in South Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of extending your home in South Melbourne? We break down costs, council fees, and factors that affect your budget — from rear extensions to second-storey additions.
body: If you own a Victorian terrace in South Melbourne or a federation home in Albert Park, a rear extension is one of the smartest ways to add space and value. But how much does it actually cost in 2026? Prices have shifted with material costs, labour rates in Melbourne's inner suburbs, and new energy efficiency requirements. A simple single-storey rear extension typically starts around $150,000, but can climb to $300,000 or more depending on size, finishes, and site conditions.

One of the biggest drivers of cost is your site access. South Melbourne is famous for narrow laneways and heritage overlays that make material delivery and waste removal tricky. If your property sits in a heritage overlay (common in the 'Golden Mile'), you'll need extra consultant reports and council permits — adding $5,000–$15,000 to the upfront design and approval stage. Always factor in a contingency of 10–15% for unexpected underground drains or asbestos removal in older homes.

The design phase is crucial. A good architect or building designer who knows the City of Port Phillip's planning scheme can save you months of back-and-forth. They'll help you maximise your floor area while adhering to setback rules and overshadowing limits. Many South Melbourne homeowners opt for an open-plan kitchen, dining, and living area with bifold doors to the garden — this layout consistently adds the most value to a property.

Structural steel is often needed for rear extensions, especially if you're removing a load-bearing wall. In 2026, steel prices have stabilised but remain high compared to pre-pandemic levels. Expect to pay around $8,000–$12,000 for a typical steel beam and column setup. Engineered timber solutions are becoming more popular as a cost-effective alternative, and they also reduce the carbon footprint of your build.

Don't forget the finishing trades: tiling, cabinetry, plumbing, and electrical. For a mid-range extension, budget $30,000–$50,000 for a new kitchen and $15,000–$25,000 for a bathroom. Stone benchtops, European appliances, and smart lighting can push that higher. Our advice: invest in quality joinery (kitchen cabinetry) and fixtures, because these are the things you touch every day and they make the biggest difference to resale value.

Timeline: a typical rear extension in South Melbourne takes 12–18 months from initial consultation to handover. Council approvals take 3–6 months depending on the complexity. Construction itself runs 8–12 months for a single-storey addition. Weather delays in Melbourne's unpredictable climate are common — factor in at least 4 weeks of buffer time. We recommend signing a fixed-price contract to protect yourself from price escalations on materials.

If you're on a tighter budget, consider a 'cosmetic renovation' instead of a full extension. Refreshing your existing bathroom, kitchen, and flooring can cost $50,000–$80,000 and still boost your home's appeal without the council headaches. But if you need more space, a rear extension is the best investment you can make in South Melbourne — just plan carefully, get multiple quotes, and choose a builder who communicates clearly.

Ready to start your extension journey? Contact Uptown Build Group for a free on-site consultation in South Melbourne. We'll talk you through feasibility, rough budget, and timelines — no pressure, just honest advice.

blogPosts.title: Bathroom Renovation Cost Guide for Melbourne's Inner Suburbs (2026)
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed guide to bathroom renovation costs in South Melbourne, St Kilda, and Fitzroy. Learn about waterproofing, tiling, fixtures, and how to avoid common budget blowouts.
body: Renovating a bathroom in Melbourne's inner suburbs is one of the most rewarding home improvements — but costs can quickly spiral if you don't plan properly. In 2026, a standard bathroom renovation in South Melbourne ranges from $20,000 to $40,000 for a full gut and rebuild. High-end finishes, larger spaces, and heritage considerations can push that to $60,000 or more. The key is to know where your money goes.

Waterproofing is non-negotiable under the National Construction Code and VBA regulations. A licensed waterproofing applicator will charge around $1,500–$3,000 for a standard bathroom, depending on the number of wet areas (shower, bath, floor). Don't skimp here — shoddy waterproofing leads to leaks, mould, and expensive repairs down the track. Always get a certificate of compliance.

Tiling is often the biggest visual element and the second biggest cost. Expect to pay $50–$100 per square metre for standard ceramic or porcelain tiles, plus $40–$70 per square metre for labour. Large-format tiles (600x600mm or larger) are trending in South Melbourne bathrooms because they reduce grout lines and look sleek. Heated floor tiles are a popular add-on — budget $1,000–$2,000 for an electric underfloor heating system.

Plumbing fixtures — tapware, showerhead, toilet, vanity — range from $2,000 for basic to $8,000+ for designer brands like Rogerseller or Astra Walker. Mixers with thermostatic control are worth the extra $200–$400 for safety and comfort. In heritage apartments, you may need to match old plumbing connections, which can add $500–$1,000 to the plumbing cost.

Vanities and joinery: custom cabinets cost $2,000–$5,000, while stock vanities from Bunnings or IKEA can be as low as $800. For a seamless look that suits South Melbourne's character homes, a custom timber or polyurethane vanity is a smart investment. Stone benchtops (engineered quartz or marble) add $1,000–$2,500. Mirror cabinets with LED lighting are another $500–$1,200.

Demolition and waste removal: $1,000–$2,000 depending on the size of the bathroom and access (stairs or lift?). Old tiles, plaster, and fittings need to be disposed of properly — skip bins in South Melbourne cost around $300–$600. If your bathroom has asbestos (common in pre-1980s homes), you'll need a licensed removalist — add $2,000–$5,000.

Timeline: a typical bathroom renovation takes 4–6 weeks from demolition to completion. Council permits are usually not required for a bathroom renovation unless you're altering structural elements or plumbing layout significantly. However, the builder must be registered with the VBA and all electrical work must be done by a licensed electrician. Expect at least 2–3 weeks of drying time for waterproofing and tile adhesive.

Want a fixed-price quote for your South Melbourne bathroom? Call Uptown Build Group. We handle every trade — demolition, waterproofing, tiling, plumbing, electrical, and joinery — so you have one point of contact. No hidden fees, just quality work.

blogPosts.title: Building a New Home in South Melbourne: A Step-by-Step Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Building a new home in South Melbourne involves heritage overlays, council approvals, and careful design. We walk you through the entire process from block selection to handover.
body: South Melbourne is one of Melbourne's most desirable suburbs, with a mix of Victorian terrace houses, Edwardian cottages, and modern townhouses. If you're lucky enough to have a vacant block or a knockdown rebuild opportunity, building a new home here can be a rewarding project. But it's not without its challenges — heritage overlays, narrow streets, and strict council controls require a builder who knows the local landscape.

First, check your zoning and heritage status. Use the City of Port Phillip's online maps to see if your block lies within a Heritage Overlay (HO). Many parts of South Melbourne, especially around Dorcas Street and the 'Golden Mile', are HO areas. This means you'll need a heritage report and your design must be sympathetic to the streetscape. A good builder or architect will guide you through this — expect 3–6 months for planning and permits.

Next, choose your building method. Traditional brick veneer is still the most common in Melbourne, but lightweight construction (timber frame with cladding) is gaining popularity for its speed and energy efficiency. Double-brick offers superior thermal mass and soundproofing but is more expensive. For a typical 3-bedroom home on a 300sqm block, you're looking at $1,500–$2,000 per square metre for a quality build.

Your design must maximise natural light and space on often narrow blocks. South Melbourne blocks are typically 8–10 metres wide. A well-designed layout might include a front living room, central kitchen/dining, and a rear courtyard or deck. Consider a first-floor setback to reduce visual bulk and comply with overshadowing rules. Many new homes incorporate a roof terrace to make the most of city views.

Engage a structural engineer early to assess soil conditions. Melbourne's soil is reactive clay, which expands and contracts with moisture — your slab needs to be designed accordingly (waffle pod or stiffened raft). This adds $5,000–$10,000 to the foundation cost but prevents cracking. Your engineer will also specify steel reinforcement for any retaining walls or deep excavations for basements, which are common in South Melbourne due to sloping sites.

Once approved, construction typically takes 12–18 months. The order is: site preparation and slab (4–6 weeks), framing and roofing (8–12 weeks), external cladding and windows (4–6 weeks), rough-in plumbing and electrical (4 weeks), insulation and plaster (4 weeks), internal finishes (8–12 weeks), and final fit-off (4 weeks). Delays are common due to weather, material shortages, or council inspections — allow a buffer.

Costs to consider: council fees ($10,000–$20,000 for building permits and developer contributions), utilities connections ($5,000–$10,000 for water, sewer, gas, electricity), landscaping ($10,000–$50,000 depending on scope), and fencing ($2,000–$5,000). If you're building with a fixed-price contract, ensure it includes provisional sums for site conditions (e.g., rock removal or contaminated soil).

blogPosts.title: Kitchen Renovation Trends in South Melbourne for 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: See the top kitchen renovation trends in South Melbourne for 2026: butler's pantries, two-tone cabinetry, induction cooking, and sustainable materials. Tips from a local builder.
body: Kitchen renovations continue to be the heart of home improvements in South Melbourne. In 2026, the trend is moving toward highly functional, beautifully designed spaces that reflect the homeowner's personality while maximising value. South Melbourne homeowners are increasingly investing in butler's pantries, integrated appliances, and warm natural materials like timber and stone.

Butler's pantries are no longer a luxury — they're becoming a standard expectation in family homes. A walk-in pantry behind a sliding door or pocket door keeps benchtops clutter-free and provides extra storage for appliances like coffee machines and toasters. Budget $8,000–$15,000 for a well-fitted butler's pantry with shelving, benchtop, and power points. In South Melbourne's narrower homes, a scullery (a compact version) is a smart alternative.

Two-tone cabinetry is huge this year. White uppers with navy or sage green lowers create a fresh, contemporary look that suits both Victorian terraces and modern apartments. Matte finishes are preferred over gloss because they're easier to maintain and hide fingerprints. Engineered quartz benchtops remain the top choice (around $600–$1,200 per square metre installed), but natural marble is making a comeback for island benches in high-end projects.

Induction cooktops are now standard in new kitchens, outperforming gas in energy efficiency, safety, and cleanliness. With Victoria's push toward all-electric homes, many builders are recommending induction even in renovations. A quality induction cooktop ranges from $1,500 to $4,000. Pair it with a downdraft extractor (if you want minimalist looks) or a powerful rangehood ducted outside — essential for open-plan living where cooking smells travel.

Sustainability is a key concern for South Melbourne homeowners. Reclaimed timber shelving, recycled benchtops (e.g., from old bridges or factories), and low-VOC paints are in demand. Energy-efficient appliances (5-star or better) reduce running costs and qualify for some council rebates. Consider under-cabinet LED lighting and double-glazed windows to improve insulation and reduce noise from busy streets like Clarendon Street.

Open shelving is still popular but requires discipline — you need to keep dishes and glasses organised. Mix open shelving with closed cabinets for a practical balance. For a typical South Melbourne kitchen renovation, expect to spend $30,000–$60,000 depending on size and finishes. A full gut and reconfiguration (moving plumbing, gas, and electrical) adds 10–20% to the cost but often yields a much better layout.

Timeline: a kitchen renovation takes 4–8 weeks from demolition to final fit. If you're keeping the same footprint and not moving any services, it can be as quick as 3–4 weeks. Always order your appliances and benchtops early — lead times are 6–12 weeks for custom stone and European appliances. A good project manager will sequence deliveries so you're never waiting.
